newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction from India stalls.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction from India stalls.

text.p: Gasoline was steady on Friday amid a lack of fresh market direction as India cancelled but reissued its June tender, traders said.
Traders had been looking towards state-owned Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) import tender which closed on May 28 and was valid until May 29 for direction.

But IOC cancelled the tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane, with a lead content of 0.15 grammes per litre, for delivery to Bombay on the west coast between June 10-14, a source close to the company said.
"It was cancelled because the lay days were too prompt," the source said.
Instead, IOC has issued a second tender for the same cargo to make up a shortfall in its system, but for later dates of June 18-22.
The new tender closes June 4 and is valid for a day.
But traders said the new dates were still very prompt.

IOC had not issued a tender since it bought 90,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery in March to the west coast at $40 per tonne over Mideast naphtha spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis or the equivalent of $1 per
barrel over Singapore 92-octane gasoline quotes, c-and-f.
In the Singapore fob market, talk was limited to an offer for 92-octane at $23.80 per barrel lifting June 22-26 while only the 97-octane was ofered at $24.70 for a cargo lifting June 14-18.
Unleaded 92-octane was last traded on Wednesday at $23.75 for June 15-20 lifting.
Naphtha was steady with June swaps unchanged at $21.85/$22.10 per barrelwith July stil in contango at $22.00/$22.20.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
